posts.name: Pulseglazer
posts.cooked:
FF Tachyon - She was amazing, nearly broken.  Even against Deadline who kept trying to shuffle her deck, she easily did the most damage.  Any damage boost at all takes her from good to absolutely insane.

FF Legacy - I didn't use his environment control much with Argent on board, but he got set up awesomely fast.  He has so many great cards that only see play late game since his deck is so strong, extra plays getting them early left him a powerhouse!

PW Argent - His new power was nice for a turn or two... but he's the Argent so once he got some instruments going, it was less amazing.The strength boosts elsewhere on the team hurt it a bit too.  I can see him being amazing with someone like A/Z, but I think I still like the PW version best.  I'm going to end up playing Kvothe an awful lot because I LOVE his new art.

Cosminfinitor - well, I smashed myself for 8 damage turn 1, but managed to survive the game at 3 hp.  He was really fun, but also really, really suicidal.  He'll be amazing against villains who wreck his toys or if you see a better power early.

FF Bunker - I tried him twice because he was so fun.  This allows me to really explore his control options, as I'm not just digging for a gun.  He's... really fun and strong in a bigger party, great for cards like Don't Dismiss Anything, PW Fanatic, and Gimmicky Character.  This is my favorite promo so far.

Extremist Sky Scraper - Another I tried twice. Game was in the Enclave, so I made SS big and just tossed endangered species at the villain all game.  The second game, I managed to switch a lot more between sizes which was super fun. I really like how just staying in normal is more viable and how many cool tricks flipping between sizes opened up.  This is a seriously complex hero though.

New Parse - She was okay... got set up really fast, but was constantly short on cards. That may be variance, but without more cards being fed, the discard is a bit tough.

 

Who have you tried and what do you think?

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
XPW Fanatic is a blast.  Esp. vs. Plague Rat.

We've messed around with Completionist Guise a bit too.

Great Completionist Guise Combos:

1.  Original Tachyon to feed the trash burst cards->FV Tachyon to put burst cards on bottom of deck->Scientific Tachyon to put Burst cards on bottom into play, then just switch back and forth between Blitz and Experiment as desired.

2.  Cosminitor to get constructs into play->XPW Cosmic to weaponize them.

3.  XPW Fanatic to use Kill the Spirit->PW Fanatic to use Resolute with the damage redirected.

There are plenty of using 1 card to get setup and another to take advantage, like FVAZ->F6AZ or Fixer->DW Fixer, but so far these three really stand out as cool uses.

posts.name: sandgoblin18
posts.cooked:
I'm telling you guys, quite possible the best team I have ever played with is Legacy, Tachyon, Guise, and Captain Cosmic.  Start with Completionist Guise for it to work, and also start with Team Leader Tachyon and Green CC to start for best effect. Those two are absolutely two of teh best heroes in the game.  For Legacy, start with whatever floats your boat/is best for the matchup.

First, after CC gets some constructs up, you can sub in XPW CC and start hammering away.  Who says CC doesn't deal damage?  Also, a note; even without Completionist Guise, green CC is good.  Like, really good.  CC can destroy his own constructs with most of his one shots, making the negative part happen less often than you might think.

Play the game as you would, jumping around with Legacy so Guise can use the powers, and also for green CC is the constructs get culled, up until Tachyon has managed to get a lot of burst in and hopefully played a lightspeed or two.  Then, sub out for regular legacy, galvanize, blitz.  A friend and I did this combo, and we have a house rule that the game doesn't end until the end of the last hero turn once the villain dies, so we can deal overkill damage just for fun.  With this combo, we ended up dealing 137 damage to Infinitor.  That's double his life, so as you may notice, more than half of that came in the final round.  We kind of cheated, in that we specifically left him with 4 life the round before, but hey, fun's fun!

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
The Naturalist promo is wicked, when you get a form.  You only cross 50% odds at 9 cards into your deck, or your starting hand plus 5 card draws.

So the longer the game goes, and the less destruction there is the better he gets.  But in those games there are other characters who do just as good, he just catapults into the Elite echelon of heroes.

He's largely invincible and does tons of stuff, but Legacy, Tempest, Nightmist, Absolute Zero Wraith all set up are in that same range.  It is just crazy seeing how good he becomes.

His real strength is when you get Rhino or Croc really early and are able to keep it.  His card draw is impressive so he has a good shot, and so while others rely on numbers of cards, Hunted Naturalist relies on getting the right card.  He can hit his peak earlier, but it requires some luck.

posts.name: Fynikz
posts.cooked:
Had our first games with the promos last night as a group:

First game was Captain Cosmic: Requital version, Completionist Guise, Extreme Prime Wardens Tempest, and KNYFE.

So... Captain Cosmic's power with Guise (any Guise) is just straight up bonkers. We were also playing at the Temple of Zhu Long, and Mysterious Ceremonies came out allowing Guise to draw 3 extra cards every turn. I'm pretty sure this should just be called "Guise Heaven".

While Guise was doing his combos, he would play "I Can Do That, Too!" to flip the next 3 cards in his deck out and play them, frequently allowing him to then play even more cards because of how Guise works. Strangly no constructs ever came out of Guise's deck to punish him :)

(I know it actually works across play areas, but Captain Cosmic kept drawing Construct Cataclysm, so he didn't have 4 in play either)

I think the villain died by maybe turn 4 or 5 and Guise had dealt the lion's share of damage. It was pretty amazing. Captain Comsi-finitor himself had a couple turns of dealing 9-12 damage with his power between Potent Disruptions, the one that deals damage by discarding his top 3, and Destructive Response. Personal massive damage is not something I ever really expected out of Captain Cosmic.

 

Second game was Skyscraper EXTREMIST, Young Legacy, Freedom Five Absolute Zero, and Tempest again vs. Akash. Zero got started pretty early and felt like a blast to play - unfortunately multiple plays of both Earth's Sacrifice and Rejuvenating Entropy (and some help from the environment) stopped him from STAYING set up, so it didn't showcase him that well. Except maybe that he's still pretty vulnerable to disruption, especially once his HP dips low enough that taking 3 fire damage is a risky move.

I thought Skyscraper would be a monster due to her scaling damage power, but Skyscraper Extremist had a lot of issues with getting her links destroyed - even though she can get them back using her normal power, it feels a lot slower than using normal Skyscraper's tiny form. She still seems really interesting, though. And hurling t-rexes at the enemy is always A+ for fun and comedy.
